result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): A gives clean, neutral copy that a designer can drop in. Its cancel and pause buttons have equal weight, and every unknown (end date, retention, resume date) is a visible placeholder. It also says to delete the pause if eng hasn't built it. B's copy is fuller, but it invents product claims, such as forwarding email receipts, 'most fixes take under a minute,' 90-day retention and a 3-day reminder email, and puts them in the copy itself. It flags only some of these in its notes, and its 'Before you go' headline adds a little friction. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): B gives clean drop-in copy with a plain heading and equal-weight buttons, and it marks every unknown fact, such as the end date, data retention and resume date, as a visible placeholder. A's copy is more elaborate but adds unsupplied details: features like forwarding email receipts, 'under a minute', a 3-day reminder email, and a 90-day retention promise in the copy that is flagged only in the notes. A also requires a reason before the cancel button. B builds the pause into the main layout, but it clearly says to remove it if eng hasn't built it.
